settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: FileUtils.resolveFile calls getCanonicalFile(), which resolves ".." and symlinks; some traversal may be collapsed before use
Exploitability depends entirely on whether a real caller feeds attacker-controlled zip entry names and whether the resolved path is later validated by the caller
expandFile/extractFile are not tied to any server request in this library; this is a utility class, not an endpoint
candidates.description: Expand.expandFile iterates the entries of a caller-supplied zip via ZipInputStream and passes each entry name to Expand.extractFile as entryName (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/Expand.java lines 112-118). extractFile computes the target as File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (line 153) and then, without confirming that f is still contained within the intended destination directory dir, creates parent directories (line 164-165) and writes entry bytes to f via new FileOutputStream(f) (line 178). FileUtils.resolveFile normalizes the supplied name and returns file.getCanonicalFile() (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/FileUtils.java lines 1308-1377); for an absolute name it returns the absolute canonical file directly (lines 1322-1336), and for a relative name such as "../../evil" it resolves baseFile+name through getCanonicalFile (lines 1365-1376). The canonical result is never compared back to dir, so an archive whose entry name escapes the destination (e.g. contains ../ segments or is absolute) can be written outside dir. Root cause: no containment check after canonicalization before opening the output stream.
missing_evidence: No in-repo caller of Expand/execute() with externally influenced archive or dest was found in the read sources

No validation of the canonical path against dir is present in the two methods read; a search of the file did not show a subsequent contains/startsWith guard, but the full call graph into extractFile was not exhaustively resolved
Runtime behavior of FileUtils.resolveFile on the host OS (separator handling, Windows drive detection at line 1322) was not executed
preconditions: A caller invokes Expand (or a subclass) with setSrc to an archive whose entry names contain traversal sequences or absolute paths
The caller supplies a destination directory via setDest and calls execute()
The process has filesystem write permission to the resolved out-of-tree location
candidates.title: Zip entry path not validated against destination in Expand.extractFile (potential path traversal on unzip)
